The gravel surface features sharp 11% switchbacks and loose stony patches that demand careful balance on loaded rigs. The 7,782-foot summit ridge offers panoramic views over the headwaters of the Mimbres River before continuing south.

name: Kelly Mesa Pass
notes: Delivers a punchy 7.4% test on the southern terminus of North Star Mesa Road where it skirts the base of Kelly Mesa. The gravel road surface is rough and rutted from summer thunderstorms with loose rocks scattering across the track. Reaching the pass concludes the grueling North Star Mesa traverse and begins the gradual descent toward Highway 35.

name: Signal Peak Divide
notes: A sprawling 7.5-mile alpine climb ascending 1,365 vertical feet along Forest Road 89, tracing the Continental Divide Trail through the rugged Pinos Altos Range. Rough doubletrack and loose rocky switchbacks with ramps exceeding 12% wind through dense fir, ponderosa, and oak woodland beneath the towering lookout tower on 8,986-foot Signal Peak. The summit crest offers sweeping vistas over the Gila Wilderness before descending toward Meadow Creek.

name: Meadow Creek Saddle
notes: Climbs out of the secluded Meadow Creek drainage along Forest Road 149 beneath the craggy summits of Scott Peak and T X Mountain. The unpaved forest road features smooth gravel through cool, shaded pine groves before breaking out onto an open saddle. The pass marks the final high-mountain divide before dropping toward the historic mining settlement of Pinos Altos.

name: Pinos Altos Crest
trail_name: NM Highway 15 (Pinos Altos Road) / Cross Mountain Road
trailName: NM Highway 15 (Pinos Altos Road) / Cross Mountain Road
notes: Ascends through the historic 19th-century gold-mining town of Pinos Altos along NM Highway 15 and Cross Mountain Road. The 5.3% grade winds past rustic log cabins and old adits beneath the distinctive peak of Cross Mountain. The 6,955-foot crest marks the Continental Divide boundary overlooking the expansive Chihuahuan desert plains stretching toward Silver City.

name: Boston Hill Ridge
park_name: Boston Hill Open Space / Silver City Borderlands
parkName: Boston Hill Open Space / Silver City Borderlands
notes: Climbs smoothly on paved and packed-gravel Ridge Road departing the southern outskirts of Silver City. The 5% incline skirts the eastern open space trails of Boston Hill, an ancient mining district noted for silver and iron prospecting. Reaching the ridge summit at 5,853 feet provides a fond final look back at the Pinos Altos mountains as the route enters the arid desert flats.

name: Tyrone Ridge Saddle
park_name: Big Burro Mountains Foothills / BLM Las Cruces District
landmark: Tyrone Copper Mine / Big Burro Mountains
parkName: Big Burro Mountains Foothills / BLM Las Cruces District
notes: A quick 6.2% dirt roller negotiating a low saddle along Tyrone Ridge Road near the sprawling Tyrone open-pit copper mine. The sandy, gravelly track winds past desert scrub, creosote, and yucca under blistering Southwestern sunshine. The crest reveals the imposing granite dome of the Big Burro Mountains rising across the western horizon.

name: Separ Continental Divide
park_name: Continental Divide Trail Corridor / BLM Las Cruces District
parkName: Continental Divide Trail Corridor / BLM Las Cruces District
notes: Crosses the low Continental Divide crest in the wide desert basin north of Interstate 10 along unpaved Separ Road. The 6% climb rolls across hard-baked caliche gravel flanked by cholla cactus, lechuguilla, and ocotillo with panoramic views of the distant Three Sisters peaks. This subtle desert divide signals the entry into the desolate, heat-scorched expanse of the New Mexico Bootheel.

name: Little Hatchet Mountain Pass
park_name: Little Hatchet Mountains / BLM Las Cruces District
parkName: Little Hatchet Mountains / BLM Las Cruces District
notes: The 177th and final climb of the Tour Divide route, rising 289 vertical feet on rough desert doubletrack skirting the base of 6,614-foot Hachita Peak. Bleaching sun, relentless headwinds, and coarse alluvial wash sand test the final reserves of endurance just 40 miles north of the Mexican border. Cresting this windblown desert pass at 5,049 feet reveals the immense Big Hatchet Mountains standing sentinel over the final descent to Antelope Wells.
